chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The visitation (of the sick) is (to last) the measure of a suckling interval of a she-camel or the milking of a she-camel.

key_terms.الْعِيَادَةُ: Al-'iyada: visiting the sick, a recommended (mustahabb) act with defined etiquette in Islamic law
key_terms.فُوَاقِ نَاقَةٍ: Fuwaq naqatin: the brief interval between two sucklings of a she-camel, used as a metaphor for a short duration

ai.seo_question: How long should a visit to a sick person last according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prescribes a brief and considerate duration for visiting the sick. The measure used — a suckling interval or milking of a she-camel — refers to a short period of time, approximately 10 to 20 minutes in the context of Arabian pastoral life. This hadith reflects the Shia jurisprudential tradition of regulating the etiquette of 'iyada (sick visitation) to ensure the patient is not overburdened while still being honored by the visit.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The visitation is of a measurement of a suckling of a she-camel or milking of a she-camel’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ’Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah from ’Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
duration of visiting a patient is as long as a baby- camel is given the chance to suckle the mother during milking the camel or as long as it takes to milk a camel.”
